headline: Washington links Ukraine's NATO membership to a withdrawal from the Donbas
standfirst: Volodymyr Zelensky says American negotiators have, for the first time, tied Ukraine's entry into the alliance to giving up the Donbas, which he refuses to do without guarantees and a referendum. Donald Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday to talk about nuclear weapons, Benjamin Netanyahu invokes the Iranian threat to demand a unity government, America loses its measles-free status, and diphtheria has killed more than 1,100 people in Nigeria this year.

essentials.title: America floats NATO membership for Ukraine in exchange for a withdrawal from the Donbas
essentials.standfirst: According to Volodymyr Zelensky, American negotiators have for the first time linked his country's accession to the Atlantic alliance to giving up the parts of the Donbas that Kyiv still holds. Ukraine's president rejects any cession of territory, but says he is ready to consult Ukrainians if offered a complete package of guarantees.
body: In remarks released by his office on Saturday 14 November, Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, said American negotiators had asked him whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, the first time, in his account, that the alliance has been tied to territorial concessions, Al Jazeera reports.

The areas in question are those Russia does not control, and Mr Zelensky refused to give them up, while saying he would put the matter to a referendum if America and its allies offered security guarantees, a funded army and a reconstruction plan; Vladimir Putin regards Ukraine's membership as a red line.

Kyiv now awaits details: Washington talks of guarantees resembling Articles 4 and 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, but with no American troops on Ukrainian soil, according to the Kyiv Independent, while the Europeans have chosen five countries to represent them in future negotiations.

figure.label: Ukrainian drones launched at Russia, according to the Russian authorities on Friday
figure.compare: with oil infrastructure among the targets

positions.wants: To know whether Ukraine would leave the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, with bilateral guarantees comparable to those Israel enjoys, but without American troops.
Guarantees from NATO and the EU amounting “at a minimum” to Article 5, a strong army and a funded reconstruction plan, before any consultation of Ukrainians.

next.t: European Council meeting, with Ukraine's financing for 2027 high on the agenda.

analysis.title: A taboo lifted in Washington
analysis.text: Since 2022 Ukraine's membership of NATO has been the one point on which Moscow will not bend, and Washington had kept it out of the talks. Tying that prospect to a withdrawal from the Donbas amounts to offering Kyiv protection in exchange for territory, a bargain Mr Zelensky does not reject outright but makes conditional on precise commitments. He nonetheless rules out neutrality, which would require amending the constitution, and refuses any arrangement that recognises the occupied territories as Russian. It remains unclear whether the American offer binds the other allies, whose unanimity any accession requires, and whether the Kremlin would accept Ukraine in the alliance, even a diminished one. Mr Zelensky himself says he is still waiting for “details”.

keys.title: The Abu Dhabi talks
keys.text: Ukrainian and Russian representatives negotiated in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November under American mediation, without a major breakthrough. A prisoner exchange involving more than 1,000 people was agreed there, according to Reuters.

keys.title: A truce offered in Kostiantynivka
keys.text: Vladimir Putin has suggested a local humanitarian ceasefire in this Donbas town, which in Mr Zelensky's view shows that the Russian army cannot take it. Ukraine's president also says the Kremlin's leader does not support a truce on strikes against energy facilities.

keys.title: Europe at the table
keys.text: America's envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, assured Mr Zelensky in Ireland on Thursday that all parties accepted a role for Europe. It will be represented by the EU's institutions and by Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland.

context.t: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Two days of Russian-Ukrainian talks end in Abu Dhabi, under American mediation.
In Dublin, the Europeans name five countries to represent them in the negotiations.
Volodymyr Zelensky reveals the American proposal linking NATO to a withdrawal from the Donbas.

essentials.title: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in Shenzhen on Thursday for a first three-way nuclear summit
essentials.standfirst: The White House has confirmed an unprecedented meeting of the American, Chinese and Russian presidents on the sidelines of the APEC summit, focused on cutting nuclear arsenals. Washington expects no agreement, and Ukraine will not be on the agenda.
body: The White House's deputy press secretary, Olivia Wales, announced on Friday 13 November that Donald Trump would meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday 19 November, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, to discuss reducing nuclear weapons worldwide, Al Jazeera reports.

The New START treaty, which capped the Russian and American arsenals, expired in February after Mr Trump declined a one-year extension in order to demand a new deal that includes China, which argues that Washington and Moscow, with far bigger stockpiles, should negotiate between themselves.

A senior American official warns that no agreement is expected and speaks of the start of a conversation, with the president due to raise the war with Iran but not Ukraine, while Volodymyr Zelensky fears a repeat of the Yalta conference and a carve-up into spheres of influence.

figure.label: since the Russian-American New START treaty expired in February
figure.compare: leaving the two biggest arsenals uncapped for the first time in more than 50 years

positions.wants: To open a discussion on cutting nuclear weapons and see China “step up”, without expecting an agreement in Shenzhen.
To let America and Russia, whose stockpiles are far larger, negotiate directly with each other, China having so far refused to put its own programme on the table.
To avoid a Yalta-style “division of spheres of influence”, according to Volodymyr Zelensky, who fears a deal struck without Ukraine.

next.t: Three-way summit in Shenzhen, after a working lunch between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

analysis.title: China, outside the arms-control treaties
analysis.text: For half a century nuclear arms control rested on a dialogue between Washington and Moscow, which hold most of the planet's warheads; China, the third nuclear power according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, has never accepted numerical limits. By letting New START lapse without an extension, Donald Trump made Beijing's inclusion a condition of any new treaty. The three-way format in Shenzhen is therefore above all a diplomatic gamble: an attempt to bring China to a table it has always avoided, on its own soil and during a summit it wanted to devote to trade. America's insistence on nuclear weapons has irritated Beijing, according to Dawn, a Pakistani daily.

keys.title: The itinerary
keys.text: Donald Trump leaves on Monday for Manila, which hosts an ASEAN summit and a meeting of Quad leaders, before flying to Shenzhen on Wednesday. He will lunch with Xi Jinping on Thursday, but no one-to-one meeting with Vladimir Putin is planned.

keys.title: The Kremlin's response
keys.text: The Kremlin's spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, called the meeting “extremely important” and rejected the comparison with Yalta. Agreements reached in Shenzhen could not, in his view, be imposed on other countries.

context.t: New START, the last treaty limiting the Russian and American arsenals, expires.
Xi Jinping visits Washington.
The White House confirms the three-way summit in Shenzhen.

Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC.

essentials.title: Netanyahu invokes the Iranian threat to demand a unity government as Washington bets on pressure
essentials.standfirst: Israel's outgoing prime minister is urging Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government with him capable of “eliminating” the Iranian threat, an offer his rival promptly rejected. American intelligence reckons Tehran still has thousands of missiles, while Washington sees no need for a fresh offensive.
body: In a video statement released on Saturday 14 November, Israel's outgoing prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, called on Gadi Eisenkot, who has been asked to form the next government, to join him in a national-unity government to remove the Iranian threat “once and for all”, an offer Mr Eisenkot dismissed within minutes, Al Jazeera reports.

The head of Mossad, Roman Gofman, met the CIA's director, John Ratcliffe, in Washington to seek American backing for new strikes, according to Haaretz, just as the Wall Street Journal, citing American intelligence, estimated that Iran retains between 1,500 and 2,500 missiles despite the bombing.

America's secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has nonetheless said fresh military action is unnecessary because the economic pressure on Tehran is considerable, while the Knesset elects its speaker on Tuesday and Mr Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, to form a coalition.

figure.label: missiles Iran may retain, according to American intelligence cited by the WSJ
figure.compare: an estimate its authors consider uncertain

positions.wants: A national-unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, without preconditions, to put an end to the Iranian threat.
A minority “national emergency government”, open to Likud provided it breaks with the supporters of Itamar Ben-Gvir.

analysis.title: The bet on economic pressure
analysis.text: Washington has so far preferred sanctions and a blockade to a new military campaign, and the Gulf monarchies, which fear Iranian retaliation, are encouraging it. The American intelligence estimate complicates that choice: even at its low end, Iran would have rebuilt more than half of its pre-war arsenal, according to a former Pentagon official quoted by Anadolu. Israel's chief worry is a deal between Washington and Tehran that eases the pressure without addressing the nuclear programme or the missiles. Israel's political calendar matters too: defeated in the election of 27 October, Mr Netanyahu heads only a caretaker government, and the general staff sees no imminent threat that would justify resuming the war in the coming weeks, according to KAN, the public broadcaster.

keys.title: The Knesset arithmetic
keys.text: Mr Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc won 53 of the 120 seats, Mr Eisenkot's 48, and the Arab parties a record 19. Mr Eisenkot, nominated by 67 members to form the government, is counting on Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties to abstain.

keys.title: A sceptical rival
keys.text: Gadi Eisenkot says Mr Netanyahu “knows he lost the election” and that his appeals do not work on him. He had not been told about the Mossad chief's visit to Washington, according to Israel's Channel 12.

context.t: War breaks out between America, Israel and Iran.

essentials.title: America loses its measles-elimination status after a string of outbreaks
essentials.standfirst: The Pan American Health Organisation has concluded that the virus is once again circulating continuously in America, a quarter of a century after it was eliminated. Experts blame falling childhood vaccination, while the administration blames its predecessors.
body: The Pan American Health Organisation (PAHO), the WHO's regional arm, concluded this week that measles transmission had become established again in America, which thus loses its status as a country that has eliminated the disease, according to researchers quoted by KFF Health News, with an official announcement due on 17 November.

Elimination requires every outbreak to die out within a year, which has no longer been the case since a cluster in Utah crossed that threshold in June, following the west Texas outbreak that infected more than 4,500 people in America and Mexico in 2025.

Robert F. Kennedy Jr's health department attributes the situation to vaccination gaps that predate the current administration, while former officials at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention say regaining elimination status is a distant prospect until the current outbreaks are contained.

figure.compare: more than 8,000 infections and 830 hospitalisations in two years

analysis.title: What losing the status means
analysis.text: Elimination status does not mean the absence of cases, but the absence of continuous transmission for more than a year: infections imported from abroad then fizzle out on their own thanks to sufficient vaccination coverage. Losing it therefore reflects the virus taking hold in under-vaccinated communities, whose share has been growing since the covid-19 pandemic, according to CDC data. To regain the status, America will have to extinguish the current outbreaks and then prevent any new chain of transmission for a year. Experts quoted by KFF Health News also point to cuts in states' vaccination grants and to delays in publishing CDC reports, which staff attribute to political appointees, a claim the health department disputes.

keys.title: The human toll
keys.text: States have reported thirteen measles-related deaths in recent months, including a seven-month-old baby in New York. The Texas outbreak killed at least sixteen people in the two countries.

keys.title: Washington's response
keys.text: The health department says it has released some $100m in additional funds to fight outbreaks. The White House insists that the president and the health secretary have repeatedly encouraged vaccination.

context.t: The west Texas outbreak spreads to Mexico and to at least three other states.
A cluster in Utah passes a year of transmission.
The American press reports the loss of elimination status.

essentials.title: In Nigeria, diphtheria has killed more than 1,100 people this year and antitoxin is running out
essentials.standfirst: The worst diphtheria epidemic on record in the country has caused more than 28,000 confirmed cases, mostly among poorly vaccinated children. Médecins Sans Frontières warns that its stocks of the only effective treatment are “dangerously low”.
body: Médecins Sans Frontières warned on Friday 13 November that its stocks of diphtheria antitoxin were almost exhausted in northern Nigeria, where its teams are already rationing treatment, as the country has recorded 28,151 confirmed cases and 1,126 deaths since January, according to health authorities quoted by Premium Times.

The epidemic, which emerged in late 2022, mainly strikes unvaccinated or under-vaccinated children in 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with Kano state alone accounting for 43% of confirmed cases, while global production of antitoxin remains limited and erratic.

The charity is calling for higher global production, faster customs clearance for medicines and sustained investment in routine immunisation, as a new outbreak is reported at a boarding school of more than 2,000 pupils in Kano state, according to Anadolu.

analysis.title: A preventable disease, a scarce cure
analysis.text: Diphtheria is prevented by a vaccine given in three childhood doses, yet about 93% of children caught up in the recent outbreaks had not received all the recommended doses, according to Muyi Aina, head of Nigeria's primary health-care agency, who blames misinformation and vaccine distrust. Once the disease takes hold, antitoxin, made from horse plasma, must be given early, because it cannot repair damage the toxin has already done, the WHO notes. Its manufacture is unprofitable and carried out by a handful of laboratories worldwide, which explains recurring shortages. In Zamfara state, only 25,000 of the 90,000 vaccine doses needed for an emergency campaign have been delivered.

keys.title: Children on the front line
keys.text: In Gusau most hospitalised patients are children, four in five of whom had never been vaccinated, according to MSF. The charity says it has treated more than 9,000 diphtheria patients since the start of the year.

keys.title: An overwhelmed public response
keys.text: In August the federal government set up an emergency task force for Katsina and Kano states, whose federal teaching hospital was overwhelmed. MSF has not confirmed that the treatment annexes announced are operating.

context.t: A diphtheria epidemic breaks out in northern Nigeria.

brief.text: Some 106,000 people, 24,000 of them in Paris, marched on Saturday against the rising cost of living at the call of the “yellow vests” and youth movements, according to the interior ministry, fewer than the week before.

President Karol Nawrocki has vetoed for a second time the law implementing the EU's Digital Services Act, arguing it would give too much control over online speech, drawing criticism from Donald Tusk.

Judges at the International Criminal Court have closed the original investigation into Afghanistan, which also covered American soldiers, while the inquiry into crimes attributed to the Taliban since August 2021 continues separately.
A global Microsoft outage, which the company blamed on a network upgrade, halted the processing of New Zealand visas and knocked out email at Japan's government.
